jobs.title: Director, Strategic Engagements (Northeast)
jobs.description: Who We Are: Xenon Pharmaceuticals ( NASDAQ:XENE ) is a neuroscience-focused biopharmaceutical company dedicated to drug discovery, clinical development, and commercialization of life-changing therapeutics for patients in need. We are looking for great people who thrive in a respectful, collaborative, inclusive, and productive culture to join the Xenon team. What We Do: We are advancing an exciting product pipeline to address indications with high unmet medical need, including epilepsy, depression and pain. Our Phase 3 azetukalner program represents the most advanced, clinically validated potassium channel modulator in late-stage clinical development for multiple indications. In March 2026, we announced positive topline data from our Phase 3 X-TOLE2 study of azetukalner in focal onset seizures (FOS), and we submitted a New Drug Application to the Food and Drug Administration in the third quarter of 2026. Our Phase 3 epilepsy program also includes a second FOS study, X-TOLE3, which would support regulatory submissions outside the U.S., and the X-ACKT study in primary generalized tonic-clonic seizures, which would support regulatory submissions for an additional epilepsy indication. We also have multiple Phase 3 azetukalner clinical trials underway in major depressive disorder (MDD) and bipolar depression (BPD), based on topline data from our Phase 2 X-NOVA clinical trial. In addition, we are proud of our strong heritage in human genetics, deep understanding of ion channel biology, and expertise in novel chemistries to enable potent, selective ion channel targeting. We continue to advance an early-stage pipeline of novel therapeutic candidates, including Phase 1 studies for XEN1701 and XEN1720 (targeting Nav1.7) and XEN1120 (targeting Kv7), which are being developed for pain. Backed by a strong balance sheet to support our growth plans, we continue to build a fully integrated, premier neuroscience company with strong discovery, clinical development, corporate, and commercial operations. About the Role: We are seeking a Director, Strategic Engagements, Northeast, to join our team. The individual will be an integral member of the Commercial team and will support commercially focused HCP engagement activities for Azetukalner. Key primary responsibility is to support key US Commercial Strategic market development strategies for the epilepsy launch. Individuals should be an exceptional business leader with deep epilepsy experience who will work Regionally to maintain: 1) KOL Engagement and 2) Uncover key market impact drivers 3) Support regional business planning across matrix colleagues. This role will ensure close working relationships with cross-functional partners in a compliant manner. This position requires close collaboration with the Commercial team, Medical Affairs and other key business partners to elevate corporate brand awareness/ advocacy. This role requires demonstrated ability to thrive in a dynamic and ambiguous environment. Position will require greater than 50% travel (can be up to 75% travel) to field-based educational events (many occurring on weekends). This includes internal meetings, advisory boards, medical meetings, and congresses. This position reports to the Senior Director, Customer Engagement, and will be fully remote. RESPONSIBILITIES: · Identify, cultivate, and maintain long-term relationships with national and regional epilepsy KOLs, advisors, and other influential stakeholders. · Own commercial KOL influence map

Our mission is simple: make really high quality essentials for really low prices, fairly and sustainably. We deliver on that mission through a unique manufacturer-to-consumer (M2C) model eliminating the layers of traditional retail that add cost and result in consumers paying more than they need to. We find, build relationships with, and work directly with the manufacturing partners behind some of the world’s finest products. From there, our teams design smart, efficient operational processes and build and deploy proprietary technology, AI, and analytics to help us scale fast. What began with a small assortment of elevated basics has quickly grown into a cross-category brand spanning apparel, accessories, home goods, and more. Today, tens of millions of people across a growing number of countries come – and return – to Quince because they trust us to deliver. OUR CULTURE Quince is a culture built for builders by builders. Our way of working starts with a blank sheet of paper. We question conventional thinking, use technology and data to uncover new opportunities, and move quickly to turn ideas into reality. Where conventional wisdom says you have to choose – soft or durable, speed or rigor, quality or price – we ask why that trade-off has to exist in the first place. Our pace is fast and the bar is high because our customers expect a lot from us and we refuse to let them down. We believe the best results come from challenging ourselves, learning from one another, and building on each other's strengths. Here, responsibility is not determined by role, tenure, or seniority. Every team member - no matter their level - has the opportunity to drive our business and shape our trajectory. If you’re someone who likes to imagine new possibilities and build better systems rather than plug-in to outdated ones, Quince is the place for you. jobs.description: About Notabene Notabene is building infrastructure that's transforming how money moves in the digital economy. We're evolving beyond our compliance foundations to enable the next generation of digital financial services between regulated institutions with unprecedented efficiency. With nearly 50 employees across 14 countries and having recently closed our Series B round last November with support from leading investors including Y Combinator, DRW, F-Prime, Jump Capital, Castle Island, and Green Visor Capital, we're looking for people like you to help shape the future rails of the crypto industry. Location: US-based, Remote East Coast. Candidates in the NYC area have a hybrid option. The impact you will have Notabene is planning on going through its first external financial statement audit, covering the fiscal years ending January 2026 and January 2027. You will own that process. You will also own the close, the books, and the accounting policy for a two-entity, multi-currency business whose revenue includes subscription fees, usage-based transaction billing, and a payments network take rate that has no clean accounting precedent anywhere. The accounting function is already substantially built. Close runs, the books are in order, and readiness work for the audit is well underway. What we need is someone to own it, finish it, and take it through the audit, while raising the standard on policy and documentation as the business gets more complex. You will be the most senior accounting voice in the company, reporting to the VP of Finance, with one direct report and a set of external providers. You will not have a large team before late 2027, and that is deliberate. Capacity here comes from better systems and better automation, and you will be the one deciding what those look like. Own the monthly, quarterly, and annual close across Notabene Inc. and Notabene GmbH. Produce GAAP financial statements, consolidations, intercompany eliminations, and FX translation under ASC 830. Technical accounting. Write the positions and the memos. We build side by side with developers, innovators and advocates, united in the belief that a better technology future is not only possible — it’s ours to create! Team One of the ways we are deepening our commitment to building side by side with innovators is Mozilla Studio: where we find promising builders and ideas, select the ones worth backing, and help them become tools and technology actually used by people and institutions. It is where the critical step from promising idea to workable, sustainable tool happens. Good public-interest technology often fails between prototype and first user, because commercial capital arrives on terms at odds with the mission, and grant capital rarely comes with the help a team needs on sustainment, supply, and operational excellence. Mozilla Studio, building on the work of our Incubator , helps to close that gap. It backs efforts early, gives teams what they need, and connects them to the deployers, buyers, and follow-on funders who help make these alternatives true defaults. Our goal is technology that lasts beyond our funding. This newly created role of VP, Mozilla Studio will hold the responsibility of building and running the Studio. You'll start with an active portfolio, including our current AI initiatives, and keep that work moving without disruption while you set the Studio's direction. This role reports directly to the CEO and partners closely with the Operations Team to steward the Studio's legal, compliance, financial, and logistical obligations, keeping handoffs clear so the Studio runs smoothly across the Foundation. This is a remote role open to candidates based in Canada, Germany, the UK, or the US. Job responsibilities As the VP, Mozilla Studio, you will… Take the helm of the Studio’s active portfolio, including our current AI initiatives. You’ll keep it moving while you build trusted relationships with the CEO, teams across the Foundation, and builders. Assess each active bet rigorously to understand who it serves, what early signals it’s showing, and what it will take to reach its next stage. Set the Studio's direction and criteria for what it backs, extends, stops, or declines, and decide how much support each team gets within our agreed investment timelines. Every decision ties back to technology people can use, held by teams that can stand on their own. Hold every bet to a clear standard: a deployer or user named up front, with progress measured in adoption and impact rather than activity. Pressure-test every commitment before capital moves to understand whether we can make a meaningful difference, and whether our risk capital can unblock something uniquely within our reach. Balance early signals across the portfolio against bigger conviction bets. Make disciplined stop decisions at the right moments and document the rationale behind each. Guide each team to a durable structure (a company, nonprofit, cooperative, mission entity, or commons project) with a working sustaining model and at least one named funder beyond us. Build and lead a high-performing Studio team and a bench of talent calibrated to support each team's stage and timeline. jobs.title: Product Marketing Lead
jobs.description: Background Nash powers the logistics infrastructure behind some of the most recognizable brands in commerce, including Walmart, Urban Outfitters, and 7-Eleven, along with platforms like Shopify and Toast. We are scaling fast, the category is forming around us, and we are building the product marketing function from scratch. We're hiring our first Product Marketing Lead to own positioning, narrative, launches, and the strategic voice of the platform that is becoming foundational to modern commerce. The Role This is the strategic seat where positioning, narrative, customer truth, competitive worldview, and launch craft come together. It is also where the next chapter of Nash's product strategy is shaped. Product marketing can take many different forms in different organizations... It can be a function to spit out whitepapers and datasheets, a megaphone for product management, or… it can be something very different: a force multiplier for the whole organization. We're looking for the latter. You'll report directly to our Chief Growth Officer (whose career has been building and leading marketing, growth, and product organizations at companies like Twilio, Plaid, and Salesforce). You'll work as a peer to our Product Team, and alongside our CEO, our CTO, and a small, senior, fast-moving cross-functional group across product, engineering, sales, and growth. The bar for taste, craft, and strategic thinking on this team is high, and the trajectory for someone strong in this seat is significant. How We Think About PMM The best PMMs sit at the intersection of three rare skills: technical curiosity, business acumen, and creativity. You don't need to be a coder, but you need to understand technical implementation, tradeoffs, and be able to talk to a technical audience credibly enough to know what they'll ask next. You don't need to be a salesperson, but you need to read buying behavior, understand the worldview of the decision-maker, and articulate the value of the problem we're resolving (not the value of our product). You talk in the language of the customer, not the language of our company. You don't need to be a designer or a copywriter, but you need to write narratives with emotional resonance, position with clear differentiation, and find the experiment, the data, or the execution model that actually moves the needle. The skills are hard enough to find in one person. The harder bar is what you do with them. Great PMM teams are not measured on what they did. They are measured on what they got the company to achieve together. They don't ask the org to enable them. They enable the org. They earn strategic influence by inspiring the company with a common vision, and then get the whole company pulling together in the same direction. How We Work: AI-Native, By Default Product marketing at Nash is AI-native and builder-led. We're looking for a PMM who has fundamentally rewired their workflow around AI, not someone who occasionally uses ChatGPT to clean up an email. Someone who reaches for Claude, Claude Code, Claude Cowork, Replit, and whatever ships next week as instinctively as they reach for a Google doc. The reason is straightforward: the speed and surface area of what one product marketer can produce has changed by an order of magnitude in the last eighteen months. Customer interview synthesis, competitive teardowns, narrative iteration, message testing at scale, launch asset production, sales enablement, internal narrative documents: every loop

Founded in 2007 and headquartered in Durham, NC, we give merchants, platforms, and fintechs a single API to connect to 150+ payment gateways and 40+ payment methods across 100+ countries, along with the intelligence to decide where every transaction should go. We're vendor-agnostic by design. Our customers choose their providers, keep their payment data portable, and never have to rebuild their stack to adopt something new. Payments are getting more complex, not less. Every new market, payment method, fraud tool, and now every AI agent checking out on a shopper's behalf adds another integration and another decision. Spreedly turns that complexity into an advantage. Our PCI Level 1 vault keeps cards and network tokens portable across providers. Smart routing and retries recover revenue lost to avoidable declines. Fraud and 3DS tools plug in with a single API call. And our payments intelligence turns transaction data into decisions merchants can act on. As agentic commerce moves from experiment to real sales channel, we're building the infrastructure that lets merchants accept agent-initiated payments through the providers they already trust. For the people who work here, that means hard technical problems at real scale, billions of dollars in annual transactions, at a moment when the rules of commerce are being rewritten. If you want ownership and work that shows up directly in your customers' revenue, you'll fit right in. About the Role Spreedly is looking for a Support Engineer to take on our most complex customer issues and bridge the gap between support and engineering. You'll go beyond identifying a bug: you'll investigate where it occurs, explain its impact, and give engineering the evidence and technical context needed to resolve it. You'll join an international support team that serves customers, partners, prospects, and internal colleagues. Our Tier 1 team provides round-the-clock support, while Tier 2 handles deeper technical investigations. This role brings additional engineering depth to that work, particularly in troubleshooting SDKs and complex payments integrations. This is a hands-on, player-coach role. You'll work directly on difficult cases while helping teammates develop their technical skills. We also want this hire to help lay the foundation for a potential Tier 3 support function. That expansion and any future team leadership role are subject to leadership approval, rather than guaranteed next steps. We expect roughly 60% of your time to focus on complex customer tickets, most of them from our top-tier accounts. The remaining time will involve retrospectives, customer advocacy, cross-functional projects, and coaching. Responsibilities Own complex technical investigations, particularly for our top-tier customer accounts. Read and navigate source code, analyze logs, and inspect API and SDK behavior to pinpoint issues. Reproduce customer issues in test environments so findings are confirmed before they reach engineering. Build clear, actionable engineering escalations that explain the problem, where it occurs, and potential approaches to resolving it, with engineering retaining final decisions on changes. Bring SDK troubleshooting expertise to support for our Checkout SDK and share that knowledge across the team in collaboration with engineering. Help manage incidents and keep customers informed, translating

jobs.title: Staff Security Engineer
jobs.description: At Beyond Finance, we've made it our mission to help everyday Americans escape the endless cycle of crippling debt and step into a brighter financial future. Through compassionate, individualized care, a culture focused on compliance and ethics, supportive user-centric technology, and customized financial solutions, we've helped over 1 million clients on their path to a brighter future. While we're proud of what we've already accomplished, we're searching for new collaborators to help us get to the next level! If you're looking to join a forward-thinking, rapidly growing organization with helping people as its number one goal, we want to hear from you. Role Overview As a Staff Security Engineer, you'll get involved early with Product and Software Engineering teams to embed security into our architecture and processes as they design, build, and ship. You'll also be someone the Security team can pull into any project, at any phase and regardless of domain, to make sure it lands on the right security outcome. This is a hands-on role, and you don't need to be an expert in all three areas: application security, cloud security, and security automation and tooling. You should have strong, demonstrated depth in one of the three, along with enough working knowledge of the other two to contribute without hand-holding and to be a trusted voice on technical decisions outside the systems you personally own. What You'll Do Partner with Engineering, DevOps, and Product across projects, providing security input at any phase of design or build, regardless of domain. Guide secure design and code review for web and mobile applications, and help manage core AppSec tooling (SAST, SCA, secret scanning, DAST, ASM, and mobile security tooling). Help triage and remediate application-level vulnerabilities with engineering teams. Contribute to cloud security posture across the AWS environment, including IAM, network segmentation, container security, secrets, and data exposure, using CNAPP and AWS-native tooling. Support cloud and application vulnerability management, and help tune WAF rules as needed. Build automation and internal tooling, primarily in Python, that reduces manual work for the security team. Contribute to security log pipelines, SIEM detections, and endpoint security controls. Help embed security checks, such as scanning and secrets detection, into CI/CD pipelines in partnership with DevOps. Contribute to secure development and infrastructure standards, playbooks, and enablement materials used across engineering. What We're Looking For Requirements 8+ years of hands-on security engineering experience. Strong, demonstrated depth in one of the following, with working knowledge of the other two: application security, cloud security, or security automation and tooling. Working knowledge of threat modeling. Operates independently and drives projects without day-to-day oversight. Nice to Have Deeper expertise across more than one of the following: application security (SAST/DAST/ASM tooling, secure SDLC), cloud security (AWS IAM, networking, container orchestration, CNAPP-driven posture management), or security automation (Python tooling, log pipelines, SIEM detection engineering). Hands-on Infrastructure as Code experience, ideally Terraform. Red teaming or offensive security experience. PCI-regulated or financial services environment experience. Mobile application security experience. AI/ML security exposure: prompt injection, data poisoning, model ab

jobs.title: Senior Data Scientist, Audio
jobs.description: Company Overview Deepgram is the leading platform underpinning the emerging trillion-dollar Voice AI economy, providing real-time APIs for speech-to-text (STT), text-to-speech (TTS), and building production-grade voice agents at scale. More than 200,000 developers and 1,300+ organizations build voice offerings that are ‘Powered by Deepgram’, including Twilio, Cloudflare, Sierra, Decagon, Vapi, Daily, Cresta, Granola, and Jack in the Box. Deepgram’s voice-native foundation models are accessed through cloud APIs or as self-hosted and on-premises software, with unmatched accuracy, low latency, and cost efficiency. Backed by a recent Series C led by leading global investors and strategic partners, Deepgram has processed over 50,000 years of audio and transcribed more than 1 trillion words. There is no organization in the world that understands voice better than Deepgram. Company Operating Rhythm At Deepgram, we expect an AI-first mindset—AI use and comfort aren’t optional, they’re core to how we operate, innovate, and measure performance. Every team member who works at Deepgram is expected to actively use and experiment with advanced AI tools, and even build your own into your everyday work. We measure how effectively AI is applied to deliver results, and consistent, creative use of the latest AI capabilities is key to success here. Candidates should be comfortable adopting new models and modes quickly, integrating AI into their workflows, and continuously pushing the boundaries of what these technologies can do. Additionally, we move at the pace of AI. Change is rapid, and you can expect your day-to-day work to evolve just as quickly. This may not be the right role if you’re not excited to experiment, adapt, think on your feet, and learn constantly, or if you’re seeking something highly prescriptive with a traditional 9-to-5. Deepgram is looking for a Data Scientist to sit at the intersection between research and data: people who think deeply about what conversational data is actually composed of, what makes data valuable, and how to best leverage that. Conversational audio presents incredibly rich scientific, engineering, and infrastructure challenges that are orders of magnitude harder than working with text. Speech carries speakers, accents, dialects, emotion, overlapping talk, code-switching, domain vocabulary, and acoustic conditions that range from a quiet studio to a drive-through — all with rich context that moves the conversation. In this role you'll collaborate closely with our research, engineering, and data teams to answer those questions rigorously and at scale. You'll care deeply about what makes conversational data difficult, you'll characterize it, and you'll shape the strategies that turn it into model gains. This role rewards conviction, creativity in approach, and a real appetite for overturning your own assumptions when the data says otherwise. This is a hands-on, high-leverage role with unusual latitude to define an area from first principles. It reports to the VP of Data Operations. We're looking for people who: See "we've always done it this way" as a starting position to argue with, not a constraint to work around Can find the one experiment that settles a question in days rather than months Are creative about where signal hides — in metadata, in model confidence, in the failures Have the vision to take a scrappy proof-of-concept and scale it 100x Are obsessed with using AI to automate and amplify their own impact W

jobs.title: Technical Support Specialist, AU
jobs.description: Nash is looking for a Technical Support Specialist to join our global, 24/7 Technical Support team. This role sits at the heart of how Nash stabilizes the platform for our enterprise merchants - owning the investigation, resolution, and clean escalation of complex platform and integration issues across our delivery orchestration system. Technical Support is Nash's intake and stabilization layer for everything beyond high-volume delivery inquiries. You'll be the person customers and internal teams rely on when something unusual is happening on the platform: a stuck integration, an unexpected provider behavior, a configuration question that needs real investigation. You'll resolve what you can, escalate what you can't with the context needed to move quickly, and help build the knowledge base that makes the next occurrence faster. This is a role for someone who enjoys the detective work of complex, ambiguous technical problems, communicates clearly under pressure, and takes ownership seriously. LOCATION Remote in Australia (required) AEST - Friday - Tuesday, 11A - 8P TRAINING 4 weeks, Monday - Friday A note on location This is a remote role, but candidates must be located in Australia. This is a hard requirement driven by contractual data access obligations with our enterprise customers, not a preference - we are not able to make exceptions. WHAT YOU'LL OWN Platform and integration investigation. Diagnose configuration questions, known error patterns, API and webhook issues, and account-specific behavior across the Nash platform. Escalation quality. When an issue needs Engineering or Enterprise Operations, you own the handoff — clear reproduction steps, investigation performed, impact assessment, and severity. Escalations from this team are expected to be actionable on arrival. Incident coordination. Serve as the active shift team for P1 incidents — coordinating communication, engaging Engineering immediately, and keeping customers and internal stakeholders informed through resolution. Proactive monitoring. Watch Datadog dashboards, alerts, and logs for anomalies and emerging risks. Surface issues before they become customer-impacting where possible. Knowledge base contribution. Document resolution patterns for novel issues so the next occurrence becomes a known pattern. Your work directly reduces future escalation volume. Overflow support. Act as overflow for Delivery Support during peak windows when issues exceed their scope. jobs.title: Customer Support Coach – Integrations
jobs.description: What Makes Cloudbeds Unique At Cloudbeds , we're not just building software, we're transforming hospitality. Our platform powers hotels across 150 countries, processing billions in bookings annually. From boutique properties to large hotel groups, we help hoteliers transform operations and uplevel their commercial strategy through a unified platform that integrates with hundreds of partners. And we do it with a completely remote team. Imagine working alongside global innovators to build AI-powered solutions that solve hoteliers' biggest challenges. Since our founding in 2012, we've continually been recognized for excellence, most recently earning top honors at the 2026 HotelTechAwards for Best Hotel Management Software and landing on Deloitte's Technology Fast 500 again, but we're just getting started. How You'll Make an Impact: As our Customer Support Coach – Integrations in Thailand, you’ll be the deepest expert at Cloudbeds on our MecX Tech integrations, principally the Carmen Accounting interface and the TM30 Immigration reporting integration. You’ll be the person Thai customers, support agents, and partners turn to when something isn’t flowing. Thai hoteliers must report every foreign guest to Immigration within 24 hours under TM30, and every night’s revenue has to land cleanly in a finance system built for Thai accounting standards. When those handoffs break, front desk teams become data-entry clerks and properties carry real regulatory risk. This is a coaching role as much as a technical one. You’ll resolve the hardest escalations yourself, then turn each one into playbooks, articles, and hands-on training that raise the floor for the whole support org, and you’ll use AI and automation to cut repetitive diagnostic work so your time goes to the hoteliers who need it. If you get satisfaction from finding the root cause, fixing it for good, and teaching others to spot it, we’d love to hear from you. Our Customer Support Team: We are a fully remote group of former hoteliers, technologists, and customer experience professionals focused on removing unnecessary manual work so we can spend more time solving the problem behind the problem and helping customers feel confident and supported. If you’re driven by curiosity and ownership and prefer deeply personalized hospitality moments over repetitive operational tasks, you’ll feel right at home here. What You Bring to the Team: Serve as the subject matter expert and primary escalation point for MecX Tech integrations, with end-to-end ownership of the Carmen Accounting interface and the TM30 Immigration reporting integration. Investigate complex failures using logs, API tooling, and structured troubleshooting until you reach the root cause, not just a workaround. Make sure Thai properties meet their TM30 obligations reliably through Cloudbeds by tracking submission success rates and driving down failures before they become regulatory exposure. Partner with Onboarding and Sales so new properties are configured correctly on Carmen and TM30 from day one. Mentor and upskill Support agents across the region on Thai integrations through training sessions, decision trees, troubleshooting guides, and ticket shadow reviews, so the team resolves more without escalating. Drive adoption of AI and modern tooling to cut diagnostic drag. Act as the day-to-day technical liaison with development and integration partners: triage jointly, escalate cleanly, keep a shared issue log, and keep resolution moving on

Extend a centralized, fine-grained, relationship-based model across the platform, replacing feature-specific permission checks with consistent, reusable primitives. Production-grade operations. What your impact will be Set the architectural direction. Bring clarity to complex decisions. Articulate the architecture clearly enough that the rest of Engineering can rally around it. Be the go-to authority. Engineers and teams building on IDSM will bring their auth questions to you, and your technical judgment will carry real influence. Raise the engineering bar. Lead design reviews, unblock engineers facing ambiguity, and champion flexible abstractions and well-thought-out interfaces. Increase velocity and reduce maintenance. Improve our architecture, including removing tech debt, so the team ships faster with less ongoing maintenance. Shape how we build with AI. Establish patterns for using AI-assisted development to deliver high-quality features faster without compromising security or rigor. Foster ownership

Data Handling & Pipeline Architect the edge vs. cloud processing split — what runs on-system under power/compute constraints versus what gets backhauled. Stand up time-series and object storage systems for sensor and telemetry data, and the ingestion pipeline that gets data from the system to backend reliable. User Interface — Configuration & Visualization Build the product configuration interface and the geospatial data visualization layer (the common operating picture) the end customer will actually use. About the Opportunity OKX is hiring a Senior Compliance Officer to build and run our global derivatives trade and transaction reporting function. The function covers CFTC swap data reporting under Part 45, EU transaction reporting under MiFIR, EU derivatives reporting under EMIR, UK MiFIR and UK EMIR, and ASIC derivative transaction reporting across multiple OKX entities and a growing derivatives product set. jobs.description: About the Role We're looking for a FinOps Data Engineer to help drive cost optimization and cloud financial governance across our AWS infrastructure and GCP footprint. You'll work cross-functionally with Engineering, Finance, and Product to find and ship savings, build the tooling necessary to maximize efficiency of every dollar spent in the cloud, and cultivate a culture of cost awareness across engineering teams. This role owns the data side of that mission: the models, pipelines, and analysis that make cost, usage, and margin numbers trustworthy across the company. This is a hands-on engineering role, not an analyst seat. You'll do the schlep work other teams don't have time for, digging into a bucket's access pattern, writing the dbt model or Python pipeline that ships the fix, building the cost-vs-revenue mart that answers a margin question once instead of every time, and chasing a number until it reconciles. Strong communication matters as much as technical depth, you'll regularly explain a savings case or a data model's implications to an engineering team, a finance stakeholder, and a leadership audience in the same week. What You'll Be Responsible For In this role, you'll: Find and ship savings across AWS and GCP: Analyze billing, usage, and cost trends to identify opportunities, rightsizing, storage lifecycle policies, data transfer, and spot/auto-scaling. Take ideas from identification through to a realized dollar figure, not just a recommendation. Build and maintain the FinOps data pipeline: Design and run the BigQuery/dbt models that turn raw billing and usage data (CUR, Storage Lens) into reconciled, trustworthy mart tables, the foundation everything else in FinOps is built on. Build cost-vs-revenue and customer segmentation models: Model unit economics and margin by product line and customer segment, and extend coverage as new products and segments come online. Apply data science to cost and usage data: Build forecasting models, detect anomalies statistically rather than by threshold alone, and quantify savings opportunities (e.g. storage lifecycle, request-cost patterns) with rigor a spreadsheet can't match. Build and maintain cost attribution: Tagging policies, cost allocation, and chargeback/showback so engineering teams can see and own their own spend. This is foundational work other savings work depends on. Automate cost governance: Build automated cost reporting, anomaly detection, and alerting. Write the scripts and infrastructure-as-code (Python, Terraform, Lambda) that enforce cost policy rather than relying on manual review. Partner with engineering on architecture decisions: Bring cost into the room early, cost-efficiencies are cheaper to get right at design than to retrofit. Work with Finance on forecasting and reporting: Support budget tracking and financial KPIs; build dashboards and self-serve analytics engineering and finance can both read. You Might Be a Good Fit If You Have strong AWS expertise and working GCP knowledge, including pricing models, billing structures, and cost optimization mechanics. Have data engineering depth: dbt, BigQuery (or an equivalent modern warehouse), SQL at scale, and data modeling for analytics (dimensional modeling, incremental models, testing). Have data science fundamentals: statistical forecasting, anomaly detection, and experimentation, and know when a rigorous model beats a rule of thumb. To achieve this, we need to make sure that our technology isn't just in the hands of big brands - we need to try to help small businesses and creative individuals too. The role Workflows are how most of the creative on Pencil gets made. A workflow is a visual sequence of steps, covering inputs, generation, brand assets, scoring, branching logic and delivery, that a person builds once and runs again whenever the job repeats, on demand or on a schedule. This role owns that product and the connections that feed it, with one goal: more workflows built and run, by more people, across every customer. You will own Workflows and Integrations. That covers the workflow builder, templates, scheduling and run management, and the steps that workflows are built from. It also covers the platform's third-party connections outside media: digital asset management systems, file storage such as Google Drive, translation services, data services such as Foreplay, and more than a hundred other business tools. You will make those connections part of the workflow itself, so that a run can start from a client's systems and deliver back into them. You will build them on a common framework, so that each new connection is quicker to ship than the last and client teams can build on it for individual clients. You will also own how workflows show up inside Scribble, our creative agent. Agents can already run as steps inside a workflow. The next step is for Scribble to find, build, change and run workflows on a person's behalf and report back as they run, and for a workflow to pause for a person's decision and act on it. You will work closely with the team that builds Scribble, and you will own the workflow experience it works through, so that a workflow behaves the same whether a person or an agent is driving it. When that works, building a workflow stops being a specialist job. Key responsibilities Own the charter for Workflows and Integrations: the durable problem, success metrics, and an explicit in and out scope list. Grow adoption across every customer, measured by the number of workflows built and run and the number of people building them. Make human review part of the run: a workflow should pause for a person's decision, record it, and continue down the right path.
